steps.observation: Work on this for 10 seconds; do not stop early. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
Here are three effective ways cities can cut carbon emissions:

1. Expand clean and efficient public transit  
   • Increase the coverage, frequency, and reliability of buses, subways, light rail, and commuter trains.  
   • Prioritize electric or hydrogen-powered vehicles and renewable electricity for transit systems.  
   • Integrate ticketing, bike-share, and last-mile connections to make public transport the easiest default option.

2. Retrofit buildings and enforce strong energy standards  
   • Require high-performance building codes for new construction (e.g., net-zero or passive-house standards).  
   • Launch large-scale retrofitting programs—insulation, efficient windows, heat pumps, smart thermostats—for existing homes and offices.  
   • Offer incentives or low-interest loans for landlords and homeowners to upgrade, while mandating energy-use disclosures to spur action.

3. Encourage low-carbon mobility and land-use planning  
   • Build dense, mixed-use neighborhoods so residents can live, work, and shop within walking or cycling distance.  
   • Invest in protected bike lanes, pedestrian zones, and “complete streets” that prioritize non-car travel.  
   • Implement congestion pricing, low-emission zones, or limited parking to discourage unnecessary private car trips and accelerate the shift to electric vehicles.
